pages.title: Bedtime Story Coloring Book Prompts for Calm Evenings
pages.metaDescription: Bedtime story coloring book prompts for five full 40-page books: a badger's lost blanket, a sleeper train, a lighthouse cat and a dream sheep.
pages.intro: A bedtime story coloring book gives the last half hour of the day a shape: color a page, read its line or two, turn to the next. Each prompt here makes a full 40-page book that tells one bedtime story from dusk to sleep, from a badger cub hunting for his blanket to a girl riding a sleeper train to her grandmother's. The five books cover ages 3 to 13, so parents and KDP sellers can pick one or list them side by side.
tips: Forty pages is a long bedtime read; color five to eight pages a night and the book lasts a week.
Give the story a clock (dusk, lamps on, moonrise, bed) so each run of pages sits later in the evening.
Selling several on KDP? Keep each book's hero and setting distinct, like these five, so the titles don't compete.

prompts.name: Bramble the badger cub's lost blanket

fields.title: Where Is Bramble's Blanket?
fields.description: Bramble, a badger cub with a white stripe and pajamas too big for him, cannot find his patchwork blanket at bedtime. He searches the twilight wood: under the fern bed, at the rabbits' burrow, the frog pond, the owl's oak, the hedgehogs' leaf pile, the fireflies' meadow and the old stone wall where the moths sleep. Each friend he visits is getting ready for bed and points him onward. At the hollow log he finds the blanket, now a nest for five baby mice. He curls up beside them, shares the blanket, and they all fall asleep under the moon.

prompts.why: Parents of toddlers get a full 40-page goodnight story that visits one sleepy animal home after another and ends with the hero asleep.

prompts.name: Noor's goodnight walk around the block

fields.title: Goodnight, Noor's Street
fields.description: Noor, a five-year-old with two puffs of curly hair and star-print pajamas under her coat, takes an evening walk around the block with her dad. They pass the baker closing his shutters, the florist bringing in buckets, the bus driver ending her last route, pigeons on the bridge rail, the corner park emptying out, a window cat, the night nurse heading to work and the streetlights flicking on one by one. Back home come bath, teeth, pajamas, a story with Dad and a last wave to the Moon from her apartment window before she sleeps.

prompts.why: City parents get a bedtime book that matches their own street, a full 40 pages that follow the walk home and the routine into bed.

prompts.name: Theo's overnight sleeper train

fields.title: The Night Train to Grandma's
fields.description: Theo, seven, red-haired and holding a stuffed rabbit called Parsnip, rides the overnight sleeper train to his grandma's house in the mountains. He finds his little cabin, eats soup in the dining car, watches fields and a sunset through the window, meets the conductor with her brass lantern, sees a sleeping town glide past, climbs into the top bunk, counts tunnel lights, spots deer by a moonlit lake and drifts off as the train climbs. He wakes at dawn to snowy peaks, and Grandma is waiting on the platform with a thermos of cocoa.

prompts.why: Grandparents and parents of early readers get a 40-page bedtime journey with a new view on almost every page and a reunion at the end.

prompts.name: Marigold the lighthouse cat

fields.title: Marigold Keeps the Light
fields.description: Marigold, an orange cat with one white paw, lives in a lighthouse on a rocky island with the keeper, Mr. Penrose. Every evening she climbs the 99 spiral steps to watch him light the lamp, then follows the beam across the sea. Tonight it sweeps over fishing boats heading in, seals hauled out on the rocks, the late ferry, puffins in their burrows, a sailboat with a torn sail that the beam guides into the harbor, a whale surfacing and the village going dark window by window. When every boat is tied up, Marigold curls up on the keeper's armchair and sleeps.

prompts.why: Parents and KDP sellers get a seaside bedtime story that fills 40 pages with boats, seabirds and harbor scenes and ends with every boat safely home.

prompts.name: Ivy and the hundredth sheep

fields.title: The Hundredth Sheep
fields.description: Ivy, ten, with a long braid and round glasses, can't fall asleep and starts counting sheep. The hundredth one, a fluffy sheep named Woolsey wearing a nightcap, stops, steps into her room and offers her a ride on a cloud. They float over the sleeping town to the dream islands: a library with pillow shelves, a night bakery making moon-shaped rolls, a river of warm milk with paper boats, an observatory where owls polish the stars, a garden of glowing night flowers and a hammock field. As the sky turns grey, Woolsey drops Ivy back on her bed, and she is asleep before he leaves.

prompts.why: Parents of older kids who resist bedtime get a 40-page dream adventure with real places to color and a story that ends back in bed.

pages.title: First Day of School Story Coloring Book Prompts
pages.metaDescription: First day of school story coloring book prompts: five full 40-page stories for preschool, kindergarten, a new school, monster school and middle school.
pages.intro: A first day of school story coloring book lets a child rehearse the day before it happens: the walk in, the cubby, the teacher, the first friend, pickup. Each prompt here is a full 40-page book that follows one hero through one first day, from a hedgehog starting preschool to an eleven-year-old opening a locker on day one of middle school. Parents, teachers and KDP sellers can choose by age or stock all five for back-to-school.
keywords: first day of school story coloring book
back to school story coloring book
tips: Follow the real day in order (morning, arrival, lessons, lunch, recess, pickup); 40 pages gives every part of the day its own run of pages.
Match the school to the child: preschool, kindergarten, a new town or middle school each have different moments to show.
List back-to-school titles in July so they rank before the August rush.

prompts.name: Hazel the hedgehog starts preschool

fields.title: Hazel Goes to Acorn Hill Preschool
fields.description: Hazel, a small hedgehog with a red bow on her quills, starts preschool at Acorn Hill. She packs a backpack with her lunchbox and a toy beetle, walks with her mom past the pond, hugs goodbye at the gate, finds the cubby with her name on it and meets her teacher, Mrs. Badger. Then come circle time, finger painting, the block corner, snack of berries, a story on the rug, nap mats, sandbox digging and the slide with Dot, a mole in big glasses who becomes her friend. At pickup she runs to her mom with a painting and a plan to sit with Dot tomorrow.

prompts.why: Parents of nervous preschoolers get a 40-page walk-through of a whole preschool day, with a friend made by the end.

prompts.name: Mateo's light-up sneakers kindergarten day

fields.title: Mateo's First Day of Kindergarten
fields.description: Mateo, five, has new light-up sneakers and a dinosaur backpack bigger than his back. On his first day of kindergarten he eats pancakes, walks to school with his abuela, high-fives the crossing guard, lines up by the red door and meets Ms. Okafor. He hangs his backpack, sits on the alphabet rug, brings his toy stegosaurus for show-and-tell, visits the library, gets lost on the way back from the bathroom and is helped by a fifth grader, eats lunch in the cafeteria, plays tag at recess and paints in art. At the gate he tells Abuela everything on the walk home.

prompts.why: Parents and kindergarten teachers get a full 40-page rehearsal of the real kindergarten day, from breakfast to the walk home.

prompts.name: Priya's first day at a new school

fields.title: The New Girl at Willow Creek
fields.theme: Starting at a new school after a move
fields.description: Priya, eight, with a long black ponytail and a backpack covered in city patches, has just moved from the city to the small town of Willow Creek. On her first day of third grade she gets on the yellow bus, finds the office, gets the wrong room, meets her teacher Mr. Hale and her class buddy Rosa, feeds the class snail, does a science experiment with magnets, eats lunch under the big oak, plays soccer at recess, helps in the school garden and joins the library's comic club. On the bus home she draws a map of her new school to show her parents.

prompts.why: Families who have just moved get a 40-page story of one new-school day that covers every hallway, lesson and friend a child is wondering about.

prompts.name: Gloop at Mossy Bog Monster School

fields.title: Gloop's First Day at Monster School
fields.theme: First day at a monster school
fields.description: Gloop, a small green monster with three eyes and one wobbly tooth, starts first grade at Mossy Bog Monster School. He rides a giant caterpillar bus, finds his classroom inside a hollow tree stump and meets Professor Grizzle, a shaggy purple teacher. The day brings roaring class, where Gloop only squeaks, puddle-jumping, cave painting, a lunch of mud pies, a slime slide at recess, a hide-and-seek game he wins because he can hide in a bucket, and music class with bone xylophones. He makes friends with Fern, a furry monster with tiny wings, and rides home with her on the caterpillar.

prompts.why: Kids who find school worries easier to face through a silly stand-in get 40 pages of monster-school moments, and KDP sellers get a funny back-to-school angle.

prompts.name: Jonah's first day of middle school

fields.title: Locker 214
fields.description: Jonah, eleven, with messy brown hair and a brand-new planner, starts sixth grade at Ridgeview Middle School. He practices his locker combination the night before, rides his bike to school, gets a schedule with seven classes, can't open locker 214 until an eighth grader shows him the trick, walks into the wrong science lab, gets a lab partner named Ana, survives a pop quiz in math, finds a seat in the loud cafeteria, tries out the clarinet in band, runs laps in gym and finds the library at lunch. At the end of the day he opens his locker on the first try.

prompts.why: Parents and teachers of rising sixth graders get a 40-page story of the whole middle school day, from schedule to locker to cafeteria.

pages.title: New Baby Sibling Story Coloring Book Prompts
pages.metaDescription: New baby sibling story coloring book prompts: five full 40-page stories of a bunny, a big brother, twins, an otter pup and an adopted baby sister.
pages.intro: A new baby sibling story coloring book gives an older child something of their own while the house fills with baby things. Each prompt here makes a full 40-page book that follows one family from waiting to the first weeks home, from a bunny painting the nursery to a nine-year-old whose family adopts a baby girl. They make a thoughtful hospital-bag gift and a steady seller for KDP and Etsy shops in the baby-shower niche.
keywords: new baby sibling story coloring book
tips: Forty pages fits the whole arc: waiting, the birth or arrival, coming home, and the first weeks of life together.
Write a separate version per family shape (big sister, big brother, twins, adoption) so buyers find the exact match.
Put the older child's own job, like singing, fetching diapers or reading, into the story's last pages.

prompts.name: Juniper the bunny waits for the baby

fields.title: Juniper Is a Big Sister
fields.description: Juniper, a young bunny with one floppy ear and a yellow sweater, learns her mama is having a baby. She watches Mama's tummy grow through spring, helps Papa paint the nursery with carrots, picks her old rattle to give the baby, sorts tiny socks, and stays with Grandma Rabbit when the baby comes. At the burrow hospital she meets her baby brother, Sprout. At home he cries, sleeps and needs lots of Mama, and Juniper feels left out, but when she sings her carrot song, Sprout stops crying. The last pages show Juniper singing to him every night.

prompts.why: Parents expecting a second child get a 40-page story for a toddler that covers the whole wait and gives the big sister a job of her own.

prompts.name: Kai becomes a big brother

fields.title: Kai and Baby Lani
fields.description: Kai, four, with black hair that sticks straight up and a favorite red cape, is going to be a big brother. He helps Dad build the crib, picks a stuffed whale for the baby and packs the hospital bag. Then he visits Mom and meets his baby sister, Lani. At home Kai fetches diapers, holds Lani on the couch with Dad's help, pushes the stroller to the park, tells her about his toy trucks, reads her a book upside down, gets bored when she sleeps all day and has a special afternoon at the zoo with Grandpa. On the last page Lani grabs his finger and Kai teaches her to clap.

prompts.why: Parents of preschool boys get a big-brother book of 40 pages, one helper job after another, ending in a first game between siblings.

prompts.name: Rosa and the twin brothers

fields.title: Double Trouble for Rosa
fields.description: Rosa, seven, with freckles and a gap-toothed grin, finds out her family is having twins. Everything doubles: two cribs, two car seats, two of every tiny hat. The boys, Leo and Max, arrive and look exactly alike, until Rosa spots the freckle on Max's ear. She becomes the house's twin expert through the busy months: double bath time, double crying at 3 a.m., a stroller as wide as the sidewalk, matching outfits mixed up, first smiles, first rolls and first foods splattered on the wall. The book ends at the twins' first birthday, where Rosa helps them blow out one candle each.

prompts.why: Families expecting twins get a rare 40-page story of the first year with two babies, told from the older sister's side.

prompts.name: Tumble the otter and the new pup

fields.title: Tumble Teaches the Pup
fields.description: Tumble, a young river otter with extra-long whiskers, wakes up to find a new pup curled on Mama's tummy in the den. The pup, called Ripple, can't swim yet, so Tumble shows her the river world as she grows: floating on her back, holding paws so the current doesn't carry them apart, diving for crayfish, cracking a mussel on a stone, sliding down the mud bank, hiding from a heron and napping in a raft of otters. When Ripple finally swims to the far bank on her own, Tumble races her home.

prompts.why: Parents of toddlers get a 40-page animal big-sibling story set on a river, where each run of pages is one skill the older one teaches.

prompts.name: Eli's family adopts baby Ruby

fields.title: Welcome Home, Ruby
fields.description: Eli, nine, tall for his age and never without his camera, learns his parents are adopting a baby. The book follows the wait: a social worker's home visit, painting the spare room, a year of checking the phone, then the call that a baby girl named Ruby has been born in another state. The family drives through the night, meets Ruby at the hospital, spends a week in a hotel waiting for papers, then flies home. Neighbors hang a banner, Grandma arrives with a quilt and Eli gives Ruby her first bath with Dad. The last pages show the photo album Eli makes of the trip.

prompts.why: Adoptive families get a 40-page story that shows their own path to a new baby, a book that's hard to find on the shelf.

pages.title: Dinosaur Adventure Story Coloring Book Prompts
pages.metaDescription: Dinosaur story coloring book prompts for five full 40-page books: a lost triceratops, a backyard hatchling, a pteranodon flight and a dino bakery.
pages.intro: Dinosaurs are one of the most searched coloring themes, and a dinosaur adventure story coloring book adds a plot that keeps kids turning pages instead of skipping around. Each prompt here makes a full 40-page book with one story from start to finish: a lost triceratops finding her herd, a boy hiding a hatchling, a young pteranodon learning to fly, a brachiosaurus baker and a summer fossil dig. They work for dinosaur-mad kids at home and for KDP sellers who want a story angle in a crowded niche.
keywords: dinosaur story coloring book for kids
tips: Name each dinosaur species in the brief so the pages draw a real triceratops or ankylosaurus, not a generic dino.
Forty pages leaves room for a journey; give the hero eight or so stops (river, volcano, fern forest) so the pictures keep changing.
Selling on KDP? A named hero and a plot set these apart from the many plain dinosaur coloring books.

prompts.name: Trixie the triceratops finds her herd

fields.title: Trixie Finds Her Herd
fields.description: Trixie, a baby triceratops with a pink frill and three stubby horns, is separated from her herd in a thunderstorm. Next morning she sets off to find them. She asks a pteranodon on a cliff, follows brachiosaurus footprints through a fern forest, hides from a T. rex behind a fallen log, crosses a river on a sauropod's tail, shares berries with a parasaurolophus family, waits out a volcano's smoke with an ankylosaurus and climbs a hill to see the whole valley. From there she spots her herd at the river. Her mother nuzzles her and the herd circles round.

prompts.why: Parents of preschoolers get a 40-page dinosaur journey with a new real species to color at every stop and a happy reunion.

prompts.name: Owen hides a hatchling named Clunk

fields.title: The Dinosaur in the Shed
fields.description: Owen, seven, with a gap in his teeth and a dinosaur T-shirt, finds a speckled egg in Grandpa's garden shed. It hatches into a baby ankylosaurus, which he names Clunk. Owen hides Clunk as he grows bigger week by week: in a laundry basket, the bathtub, a wheelbarrow, the treehouse, then under a tarp in the backyard. Clunk eats the tomato plants, chases the mail truck, smashes the birdbath with his club tail and turns up at the school bus stop. Grandpa finally finds out and shows Owen a glowing door at the back of the shed. Together they walk Clunk home to a Cretaceous swamp.

prompts.why: Parents of early readers get a funny 40-page story of a dinosaur loose in a modern town, with something new for Clunk to wreck on every spread.

prompts.name: Wren the pteranodon learns to fly

fields.title: Wren Takes to the Sky
fields.description: Wren, a young pteranodon with a crooked orange crest, is the last chick in her cliff nest who can't fly. She practices flapping on the ledge, tumbles into the sea, gets fished out by a plesiosaur and tries again. When she finally glides, she follows the coast: over a beach of hadrosaur nests, a herd of triceratops at a river mouth, a sauropod wading in a lagoon, a T. rex on a sand bar, a volcano island and a storm she rides out on an updraft. On the last pages she catches her first fish and lands back at the cliff, where her family is waiting.

prompts.why: Kids who love flying reptiles get 40 pages of a coastline seen from above, and KDP sellers get a pteranodon hero that stands out in the dinosaur niche.

prompts.name: Bronte the brachiosaurus bakery

fields.title: Bronte's Dinosaur Bakery
fields.description: Bronte, a brachiosaurus in a striped apron, runs the bakery at the top of Fern Valley, using her long neck to reach the high oven. On the morning of little Stego's birthday she bakes a seven-layer volcano cake and sets off to deliver it. On the way she gives a loaf to the triceratops farmers, muffins to the ankylosaurus road crew, buns to the pteranodon mail carriers, and pies to the duck-billed dinosaurs at the lake. A rainstorm nearly washes the cake away, but a T. rex holds a giant leaf over it. Bronte arrives just in time, and the whole valley sings to Stego.

prompts.why: Parents of toddlers get a 40-page dinosaur story with no scary bits, just deliveries, friendly species and a birthday party.

prompts.name: Sora's summer fossil dig

fields.title: The Badlands Dig
fields.description: Sora, eleven, in a wide-brimmed hat and dusty boots, spends the summer with her aunt, a paleontologist, at a dig in the badlands of Montana. They set up camp, hike the gullies looking for bone fragments, and Sora spots a weathered vertebra sticking out of a hill. The team maps the site, brushes away rock, uncovers a hip, a leg and a skull with three horns, wraps the bones in plaster jackets, survives a hailstorm and lifts the jackets out by helicopter. At the museum lab, preparators clean the bones, and on the last page Sora stands under the mounted triceratops with her name on the sign.

prompts.why: Older dinosaur fans and science teachers get 40 pages that follow a real dig step by step, from first bone to museum display.

pages.title: Space Adventure Story Coloring Book Prompts
pages.metaDescription: Space story coloring book prompts for five full 40-page books: a teapot rocket to the Moon, a planet rally, an alien on a farm and a Mars dust storm.
pages.intro: A space adventure story coloring book turns the solar system into a journey: each run of pages is a new planet, moon or rescue. Each prompt here makes a full 40-page book with one story, from a mouse flying a teapot rocket to the Moon to a twelve-year-old saving the greenhouse on a Mars base. They suit space-mad children, teachers adding a story to a science unit and KDP sellers in the space niche.
keywords: space story coloring book for kids
tips: Make each stop a real place (the Moon, Mars, Saturn's rings, Europa) so the book teaches a little while it tells the story.
A 40-page planet tour has room for every planet plus takeoff and landing; list the stops in order in the brief.
Bring the hero home on the last pages; a trip that returns feels finished.

prompts.name: Luna-Mae's teapot rocket to the Moon

fields.title: Luna-Mae Goes to the Moon
fields.theme: A mouse flies to the Moon
fields.description: Luna-Mae, a small grey mouse in a knitted helmet, wants to know if the Moon is made of cheese. She builds a rocket from a teapot, a thimble and two spoons, counts down and blasts off from the kitchen windowsill. She floats past the clouds, a satellite and a sleepy comet, lands in a crater, bounces in low gravity, finds old astronaut footprints and a parked rover, digs in the grey dust, sees Earth rise over the horizon and tastes a moon rock: not cheese. She flies home, lands in the sugar bowl and has cheese on toast for supper.

prompts.why: Parents of preschoolers get a funny 40-page first trip to the Moon with real lunar sights and a cozy ending at home.

prompts.name: Kofi and Bolt's solar system rally

fields.title: The Great Planet Rally
fields.description: Kofi, eight, in an orange spacesuit, and his robot dog Bolt enter the Great Planet Rally: visit every planet, collect a stamp at each and get back to Earth first. They launch from the school field, skim scorching Mercury, peek under Venus's clouds, race a dust storm on Mars, weave through the asteroid belt, circle Jupiter's Great Red Spot, slide along Saturn's rings, roll past tilted Uranus, ride Neptune's winds and wave to Pluto. Bolt's battery dies near Neptune and Kofi pedals the backup power. They land second, with the only full stamp card.

prompts.why: Teachers and parents of planet-mad kids get a 40-page solar system tour in planet order, wrapped in a race story.

prompts.name: Blip the alien lands on Grandma's farm

fields.title: Blip Lands on the Farm
fields.description: Blip, a small green alien with three antennae and a round silver ship, crash-lands in Grandma Rose's cornfield. Twins Ava and Sam find him and show him Earth things: a cow that moos and makes him jump, the chicken coop, a tractor ride, a puddle to splash in, an apple off the tree, a bubble bath and a bedtime story. Blip shows them how his antennae glow. Then the three of them fix his ship with a tractor part, a colander and Grandma's sewing kit. At sunset Blip lifts off, and that night the twins see a new star blinking from their window.

prompts.why: Parents and grandparents of young kids get a 40-page space story set mostly on a farm, so it pairs a familiar world with a visitor from the stars.

prompts.name: Tessa and the Mars dust storm

fields.title: Dust Storm on Mars
fields.description: Tessa, twelve, with a shaved head and a patched red jumpsuit, is one of the first kids living at Ares Base on Mars. The book shows her days: school over video from Earth, tending tomatoes in the greenhouse dome, riding the rover to the ice mine, watching blue Martian sunsets. Then a dust storm buries the solar farm and the greenhouse starts to freeze. Tessa and her friend Dev drive the rover through the storm, dig out the panels, reroute a cable and get the heaters running. When the dust clears, the base gathers in the greenhouse to eat the first ripe tomatoes.

prompts.why: Older space fans and STEM teachers get a 40-page story of daily life on Mars with a rescue that runs on real Martian dangers.

prompts.name: Zip the comet postman

fields.title: Zip Delivers the Mail
fields.theme: Delivering post around the solar system
fields.description: Zip, a young comet with a long ice tail and a mailbag, delivers postcards to the moons of the solar system. He loops out from the Sun past Earth's Moon, drops a parcel at the craters of Mercury, sorts letters on Mars's tiny moon Phobos, rings the bell on volcanic Io, skates over the ice of Europa, slides a package under Titan's orange haze, visits the geysers of Enceladus and pushes on to icy Triton. The last letter has no address. Zip follows the clues across space and delivers it to a lonely rock beyond Pluto, then turns for home, his tail lighting up behind him.

prompts.why: Kids who already know the planets get 40 pages of real moons, and teachers get a story they can use alongside a lesson on the outer solar system.

pages.title: Kindness and Friendship Story Coloring Book Prompts
pages.metaDescription: Kindness and friendship story coloring book prompts: five 40-page stories of a lonely porcupine, a kindness map, a rain cloud and two science fair rivals.
pages.intro: A kindness and friendship story coloring book shows social skills the way children learn them, by watching a character do it. Each prompt here makes a full 40-page book with one story, from a porcupine who can't hug to two eleven-year-old rivals stuck on the same science project. Teachers use these for social-emotional learning, parents use them to talk about friends and sharing, and KDP sellers find steady demand in the character-building niche.
tips: Show kindness as small, copyable actions (carrying groceries, sharing a ball) on their own pages.
A 40-page story gives a friendship time to grow; show the first meeting, a few setbacks and the day they become friends.
Teachers buy these for SEL lessons; a book with one scene per page gives the class something to talk about on every page.

prompts.name: Pickle the porcupine wants a hug

fields.title: Nobody Hugs a Porcupine
fields.description: Pickle, a young porcupine with a green scarf, moves to Maple Meadow and wants to make friends, but her quills get in the way. She pops the rabbits' balloons, gets stuck to the squirrels' tug-of-war rope and pricks the mole at the picnic. She tries wearing a pillow, a pot and a coat of leaves. Then she uses her quills to pick up all the apples after a windstorm, holds up the frogs' tent in the rain and spikes the paper lanterns for the meadow party. At the party a tortoise with a hard shell gives her the first hug, and then everyone hugs her with oven mitts.

prompts.why: Parents and preschool teachers get a funny 40-page friendship story where the hero's odd trait ends up helping the whole meadow.

prompts.name: Amara's neighborhood kindness map

fields.title: Amara's Kindness Map
fields.theme: One kind act at a time
fields.description: Amara, seven, with braids tied in yellow beads, draws a map of her block and plans one kind thing for every house in a single Saturday. She carries Mrs. Kim's groceries, waters Mr. Lopez's tomatoes, chalks a hopscotch for the twins, walks a puppy for a man on crutches, returns a lost cat, leaves a drawing for the mail carrier, bakes muffins with her mom for the fire station and reads to a neighbor at the senior home. By evening the map is full of stars, and the whole block surprises her with a street picnic at sunset.

prompts.why: Teachers and parents get a 40-page book of real, copyable kind acts in a real neighborhood, with a clear one-act-per-house structure.

prompts.name: Yusuf and June's recess game

fields.title: The Game With No Words
fields.description: Yusuf, eight, has just arrived from far away and speaks no English yet; he wears a blue knit cap and carries a worn soccer ball. June, eight, with short red hair and a cast on her arm, can't play tag at recess. On Monday Yusuf shows her a game with a ball and five stones. Through the week they teach each other words with drawings and pointing: ball, sun, lunch, sister, funny. They swap lunches, make up a handshake, get lost on a field trip together and find their way back. On Friday they teach the stone game to the whole class.

prompts.why: Teachers with new-to-English students and families who've moved get a 40-page school-week friendship story built on actions, not words.

prompts.name: Puff the little rain cloud

fields.title: Puff Gives Away the Rain
fields.description: Puff, a small round cloud with a curl on top, drifts across the valley one hot summer day. She makes shade for a tired cow, rains on a dry vegetable garden, cools a dog on a sidewalk, fills a bird bath, waters a sunflower field and puts out a farmer's runaway bonfire. With every gift she gets smaller, until she is just a wisp over the lake. The lake breathes mist back up to her, the wind brings her cloud friends, and she grows big again. On the last page the sun comes out behind her and a rainbow stretches over the whole valley.

prompts.why: Parents of toddlers get a 40-page story told through weather, one helpful act per page, that ends with a rainbow to color.

prompts.name: Maya and Dev's science fair

fields.title: Partners by Accident
fields.description: Maya and Dev, both eleven and both sure they're the best at science, get paired for the school science fair. Maya has a high ponytail and a notebook full of lists; Dev wears a hoodie and builds things from junk. They argue about the topic, then agree on a solar oven. Over six weeks the oven melts, catches fire, blows off the garage roof in a storm and finally works. They test it on cookies, s'mores and a pizza, nearly miss the deadline when Dev's bike chain snaps, and present together. They win honorable mention and plan next year's project on the bus home.

prompts.why: Middle-grade readers and teachers get a 40-page friendship story with a hands-on project at its center, a fit for tweens who have outgrown animal stories.

pages.title: Christmas Story Coloring Book Prompts for Kids
pages.metaDescription: Christmas story coloring book prompts for five full 40-page books: a kitchen mouse, a reindeer in training, a lost letter, a snowman night and a tree farm.
pages.intro: A Christmas story coloring book is a stocking-stuffer that keeps kids busy on the slow days before the holiday and gives them a story to read on Christmas Eve. Each prompt here makes a full 40-page book with one original holiday story, from a mouse decorating a kitchen in secret to an eleven-year-old running the family tree farm. They are safe to sell, a seasonal bestseller for KDP and Etsy shops, and a family favorite for advent.
keywords: Christmas story coloring book for kids
tips: Publish Christmas titles by October; KDP holiday search traffic peaks in November.
Use original holiday characters; famous reindeer and film snowmen are trademarked.
Forty pages fits an advent read: color one or two a day through December and finish on Christmas Eve.

prompts.name: Nutmeg the kitchen mouse decorates

fields.title: Nutmeg's Secret Christmas
fields.theme: A mouse's Christmas in the kitchen
fields.description: Nutmeg, a tiny brown mouse in a red knitted hat, lives behind the kitchen wall of the Baker family's house. While the family sleeps in December, she decorates in secret: strings cranberries along the shelf, hangs a thimble bell, builds a gingerbread cottage from crumbs, wraps a walnut as a present and stitches a stocking from a sock. She rides the toy train around the tree, sledges down the banister on a spoon and hides from the cat. On Christmas morning the Baker children find a tiny stocking by the mouse hole, and they leave a crumb of cake inside for Nutmeg.

prompts.why: Parents of preschoolers get a cozy 40-page Christmas story full of small house details, safe to sell because the hero is original.

prompts.name: Thistle the reindeer trains for the sleigh

fields.title: Thistle Joins the Team
fields.description: Thistle, a young reindeer with one crooked antler and a jingle collar, enters flight school at the North Pole to join the sleigh team. Training brings take-off practice on the ice runway, a crash into the snowman orchard, loop-the-loops over the elf village, night flying by lantern, rooftop landings on the workshop and a harness relay against the older reindeer. Thistle keeps finishing last. On Christmas Eve a blizzard grounds the team, but Thistle's crooked antler catches the wind just right, and she leads the sleigh through. The book ends with her name stitched on a stall.

prompts.why: Families and KDP sellers get a 40-page original reindeer story that takes the reader through a full season of training to Christmas Eve.

prompts.name: Wilbur the penguin and the lost letter

fields.title: The Last Letter to the North Pole
fields.description: Wilbur, a penguin postmaster in a blue cap, runs the North Pole Post Office. In December the letters pour in: by plane, by boat, by sled. He sorts them into mountains, stamps them and loads the elves' carts. On December 23 he finds one letter that slipped behind a mailbag, from a girl named Hana asking for her grandfather's lost music box to be found. Wilbur sets off by dog sled, crosses an iced-over lake, borrows a lantern from a lighthouse keeper, searches a toy-repair shop and finds the music box. He delivers it to the workshop just as the sleigh takes off.

prompts.why: Parents and teachers get a 40-page Christmas mystery with a post office, a journey and a deadline, a different shape from the usual Santa story.

prompts.name: Sofia and Max's snowman night

fields.title: Captain Carrot's Christmas Eve
fields.description: Sofia and Max, a sister and brother in matching striped hats, build a snowman on Christmas Eve and name him Captain Carrot. After they fall asleep, Captain Carrot wakes up and wanders the town: he skates on the icy pond, rides the carousel at the Christmas market, sings with the carolers, helps the baker deliver pies, rings the church bell, waves at the late train and sits under the big town tree. Near dawn the children wake and run outside. Captain Carrot is back in the yard, wearing a new scarf, with a candy cane in his hand.

prompts.why: Parents of young children get a 40-page Christmas Eve story that visits every corner of a snowy town and ends on Christmas morning.

prompts.name: Hattie runs the Christmas tree farm

fields.title: Hattie's Tree Farm Week
fields.description: Hattie, eleven, in a plaid jacket and work gloves, has to run her family's Christmas tree farm for the last week before Christmas when Grandpa breaks his arm. She tags trees with families, drives the hay wagon, ties trees to car roofs, keeps the bonfire going, sells cocoa at the stand, rescues a lost dog in the pines, fixes the jammed tree baler and wraps wreaths in the barn. On Christmas Eve she and Grandpa deliver a free tree to the children's hospital and decorate it with the kids. The book ends with the family's own tree, cut last, lit up in the farmhouse window.

prompts.why: Older kids and KDP sellers get a 40-page Christmas story set on a real tree farm, with chores and an Eve delivery rather than elves.

pages.title: Ocean Adventure Story Coloring Book Prompts
pages.metaDescription: Ocean story coloring book prompts for five full 40-page books: a lost seahorse, a humpback calf, a bottle message, a deep sea dive and a hermit crab.
pages.intro: An ocean adventure story coloring book takes kids from the beach to the deep sea, with coral reefs, kelp forests and shipwrecks to color along the way. Each prompt here makes a full 40-page book with one story, from a baby seahorse lost on the reef to a twelve-year-old diving to the ocean floor in a research sub. They suit ocean-loving kids, summer travel bags and KDP sellers in the sea-life niche.
keywords: ocean story coloring book for kids
under the sea story coloring book
tips: Move the story through real ocean zones (tide pool, reef, kelp forest, open sea, deep sea) so every few pages look different.
Name the sea creatures in the brief: a manta ray, a moray eel, an anglerfish.
Summer and beach-vacation buyers peak in May and June; a 40-page book lasts a whole beach week.

prompts.name: Bubbles the seahorse finds her dad

fields.title: Bubbles Finds Her Way
fields.description: Bubbles, a baby seahorse with a curly pink tail, drifts away from her dad in a strong current on the coral reef. She sets off to find him and asks everyone she meets: a clownfish in an anemone, a sea turtle napping on a ledge, a grumpy pufferfish, a moray eel in a crack, a family of shrimp at a cleaning station, an octopus who changes color, a parrotfish crunching coral and a ray gliding over the sand. Each points her a little farther. At the seagrass meadow she finds her dad holding onto a blade of grass, waiting, and she curls her tail around his.

prompts.why: Parents of preschoolers get a 40-page reef journey with a new named sea animal on nearly every page and a reunion at the end.

prompts.name: Juno the humpback calf's migration

fields.title: Juno's Long Swim
fields.description: Juno, a humpback whale calf with one white flipper, is born in a warm lagoon. In spring she and her mother swim north thousands of miles to the cold feeding grounds. On the way Juno practices breaching, races spinner dolphins, rests over a coral bank, passes a container ship, hides from orcas behind her mother, sees sea lions on a buoy, swims under a fishing boat, meets other whales singing in the deep and crosses the open ocean in a storm. At the cold waters she sees icebergs and swarms of krill, and joins the adults blowing bubble nets to feed.

prompts.why: Kids who love whales and teachers covering migration get a 40-page story that follows a real route from a warm lagoon to cold northern seas.

prompts.name: Finn's message in a bottle

fields.title: Finn and the Bottle Message
fields.description: Finn, eight, with sun-bleached hair and a striped life jacket, finds a bottle on the beach with a hand-drawn map inside. He and his grandpa sail their small boat, the Pelican, to follow it. They stop at a lighthouse island, a sandbar full of seals, a mangrove with a heron's nest, a reef they snorkel over, a cove with a shipwreck and a fishing village where an old woman recognizes the map: she drew it as a girl seventy years ago. The last mark leads to a tin of her childhood treasures buried under a palm. Finn adds his own drawing and they bury it again.

prompts.why: Parents and grandparents get a 40-page sea adventure with islands, boats and a treasure hunt, and no pirates.

prompts.name: Amaya's dive to the ocean floor

fields.title: Down to the Abyss
fields.description: Amaya, twelve, with a braid tucked into a ship's cap, joins her mother's research crew for a dive in the submersible Kestrel. They sink through the zones: the sunlit zone with tuna and jellyfish, the twilight zone with lanternfish and a giant squid's eye in the dark, the midnight zone with an anglerfish and a vampire squid, then the abyss with sea pigs and glass sponges. At the bottom they reach a hydrothermal vent with tube worms and white crabs, and Amaya spots a sea cucumber no one has seen before. Back on deck, the scientists name the new species after her.

prompts.why: Older ocean fans and science teachers get a 40-page dive through every ocean zone with real deep-sea animals at each depth.

prompts.name: Pearl the hermit crab's new shell

fields.title: Pearl Needs a New Shell
fields.description: Pearl, a hermit crab with purple legs and one big claw, has grown too big for her snail shell. She sets off across the tide pools to find a new home. She tries a bottle cap, a teacup washed up on the sand, a toy bucket, a coconut, an old boot, a sea urchin's empty shell and a jar, and every one is too big, too small, too heavy or too leaky. She asks a starfish, a sea anemone, a gull and a lobster for help. At the edge of the rocks she finds a whelk shell that fits just right, and she gives her old shell to a smaller crab.

prompts.why: Parents of toddlers get a funny 40-page tide pool story where every page is one more shell to try.
